content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps forward: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). 2) Doebner modification to make α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. 3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic steps: target -> disconnect amide bond between C(=O)N and aromatic amine (aniline). So precursor: α,β-unsaturated acid (with phenyl amide)?? Actually target has amide: C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So break that: give acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid is: /C=C/C(=O) (attached to phenyl sulfonyl). Actually the acid part is: /C=C/C(=O) attached to sulfonyl phenyl? Wait structure: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So phenyl ring (c2) substituted with α,β-unsaturated amide side chain. The amide carbonyl attached to aniline (c3). So acid precursor would be the α,β-unsaturated acid: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to phenyl sulfonyl? Actually the carbonyl is part of amide, so acid would be /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to phenyl sulfonyl (i.e., the same phenyl-sulfonyl group). So precursor acid: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait need to think.

Better: target: phenyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring (c1) with methyl. The sulfonyl attached to second phenyl (c2) which has side chain /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N (an aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to aniline (which also has NH2). So the amide carbonyl is attached to aniline nitrogen (makes N-aryl amide). So the acid precursor would be the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to sulfonyl phenyl: /C=C/COOH attached to phenyl-sulfonyl.

Thus step 1 retrosynthesis: disconnect amide -> give α,β-unsaturated acid (call A) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Step 2: disconnect α,β-unsaturated acid via Doebner modification: precursor aldehyde (aromatic aldehyde) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So aldehyde would be the aromatic aldehyde attached to sulfonyl phenyl: i.e., c2 phenyl with aldehyde at position where side chain attaches. So aldehyde: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl phenyl. So we need aldehyde precursor B.

Step 3: disconnect sulfonyl phenyl via sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride + aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). Actually sulfonamide formation is between amine and sulfonyl chloride. In target, sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl (c1) with methyl. The nitrogen is attached to sulfonyl group and to phenyl (c1). So the amine precursor is the aniline (c1 with methyl) i.e., p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline). The sulfonyl chloride precursor is the sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl (c2) with sulfonyl group attached (i.e., 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl ring that later becomes aldehyde after Doebner. So sulfonyl chloride is p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride attaches to the first phenyl (c1) via nitrogen. The sulfonyl chloride is derived from the second phenyl (c2) which has the aldehyde substituent later. So sulfonyl chloride precursor: p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (i.e., 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride). That after Doebner gives aldehyde? Actually Doebner uses aldehyde as substrate, not sulfonyl chloride. So we need aldehyde (p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride?) No, the aldehyde is on the phenyl ring that also bears sulfonyl chloride? The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring; the aldehyde is a substituent on same ring. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride. After sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine, we get sulfonamide attached to phenyl with aldehyde substituent. Then Doebner modifies that aldehyde to α,β-unsaturated acid. Then amide coupling attaches aniline.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Step 3 (most retro): sulfonamide formation: target -> disconnect N-S bond to give p-toluidine (SMILES: Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride (SMILES: O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccc(C=O)cc1). Step 2: Doebner modification on the aldehyde part: 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride? Wait Doebner uses aldehyde + malonic acid to give α,β-unsaturated acid. The sulfonyl chloride is not compatible; we need aldehyde without sulfonyl chloride. Actually after sulfonamide formation, the sulfonyl group is already attached to nitrogen, so the sulfonyl chloride is consumed. The aldehyde remains on the aromatic ring attached to sulfonyl group. So the Doebner step should be applied to the aromatic aldehyde (attached to sulfonyl group) to give the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to sulfonyl group. So the precursor for Doebner is the sulfonamide (with aldehyde) and malonic acid. But we are doing retrosynthesis, so we disconnect the C=C bond formed in Doebner, giving aldehyde (still attached to sulfonamide) and malonic acid. So step 2: disconnect α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde (still attached to sulfonamide) + malonic acid. So we need template for Doebner modification.

Step 1: amide formation disconnect amide to give α,β-unsaturated acid (with sulfonamide) and aniline.

Thus final route: target -> (step1) amide formation reverse -> precursor1 (α,β-unsaturated acid sulfonamide) + aniline. Then (step2) Doebner reverse -> precursor2 (aldehyde sulfonamide) + malonic acid. Then (step3) sulfonamide reverse -> p-toluidine + 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride.

We need to produce JSON with nested reactions.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We can search for templates matching these transformations.

First, amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Search for templates where functional_groups_broken includes aliphatic carboxylic acid and formed amide. Use functional_groups_formed: amide. Let's search.
